steps.step: seed: user, 5 synced schedules (1 passcode), 1 completed recovery, 2 pending recoveries (escrow pending)
backup: quiesce MAIN + worker + Meet, dump both databases, archive MAIN data volume
DISASTER: destroy MAIN stack + volumes and Meet database container
restore: fresh Meet PostgreSQL, fresh MAIN PostgreSQL, MAIN data volume, services

checks.name: backup artifacts contain no key material or secrets
restored MAIN data volume: pre-disaster session still valid
schedules restored consistently (JSON volume and PostgreSQL agree)
checks.detail: restored=6, marker absent in both stores

checks.name: legacy codes still resolve to the same meetings
post-restore host authentication with vaulted secrets
completed recovery (acked pre-backup) host secret still valid
pending encrypted escrow recoverable after restore (same request replays same secret)
wrong RECOVERY_ESCROW_KEY cannot decrypt escrow (fails closed, no secret leaked)
correct key (from secure backup) recovers the escrow
restored sync worker completes outstanding acknowledgments; no escrow left pending
audit log preserved and sequence continues (no id reuse)
schedule reconciliation works after restore (edit + new schedule sync)

objectives.note: RPO measured here is only the gap between this drill's backup and the simulated disaster. No automated backup schedule exists yet, so the RPO the product can actually guarantee is undefined until one is configured.
